description_full: Cellebrite DI Ltd. develops software and services for legally sanctioned investigations in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Americas, and the Asia-Pacific. The company provides a platform of software solutions used to access, collect, review, extract, decode, decrypt, analyze, share and manage digital evidence across the investigative lifecycle for a range of investigations, such as child exploitation, homicide, anti-terror, border control, sexual crimes, organized crime, human trafficking, corporate security, and intellectual property theft, as well as financial crimes, including those involving cryptocurrency. It also offers Inseyets, digital forensics software that collects and reviews digital evidence from various digital sources when conducting legally sanctioned investigations; Guardian Forensics, an evidence management solution which enables customers to manage their digital forensics workflows, and to store, share and review digital evidence; Guardian Collaborate, a digital evidence sharing tool; and Guardian Investigate, a case management and AI-powered analytics solution. In addition, it provides Cellebrite Pathfinder, which reduces the time spent manually reviewing digital evidence and enables actionable insights into a range of crime types; Corellium Falcon for conducting mobile vulnerability research, exploit introspection, and malware analysis; and Corellium Viper for mobile application penetration testing capabilities. Further, the company offers professional services, such as training and certification services, and advanced services. It serves federal, state, and local agencies, as well as corporations and service providers. The company is headquartered in Petah Tikva, Israel.
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $370K ranks in the below the sector median among Technology peers, improving at 18%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $125K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $35K per employee reflects an ownership culture.
financial_summary: Cellebrite DI Ltd. is a mid-cap technology business with a $3.1B market cap on $476M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +25% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 90% against a 10% cost of capital — a 80-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 84% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $160M in free cash flow — roughly 34 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.22× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -10.1% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 44% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

prof: ROIC of 90% clears the cost of capital of 9.6% by 80pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.69).
It runs a 84% gross margin and converts 34% of revenue into free cash flow, or 24% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 2.22x, but high accruals (-10.1% of assets).
ROE of 16% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $276.0M (9% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 5.0, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 24.5% over 3 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.14 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 85% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 25%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 2.8% of sales), a maintenance pace.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 7.6% on average.
own: Insiders own 44.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 54%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (8 sales, net $2.8M sold).
The share count has grown 14.8% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 1,285 employees, each generates about $370K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and productivity has risen 17.9% a year.
That works out to $125K of free cash flow per employee.
